title: Arne · Living the ordinary days
orientation: Twelve linked moments about daily life after Ingrid’s death. Use the prompted skill, give feedback and retry. Each next scene is a new moment, not a response to your exact words.

scenes.bridge: A morning in the familiar kitchen.
scenes.prompt: Reflect the loss in this ordinary moment.
scenes.text: [Quietly] I still put two cups out. Seeing hers empty makes me sad.
scenes.suggestion: That empty cup brings home how much you miss having Ingrid beside you.

scenes.bridge: Arne asks what exploring a routine could offer.
scenes.prompt: Explain a small, optional way to explore the moment.
scenes.text: [Puzzled] Why talk about the empty cup? I know perfectly well she’s gone.
scenes.suggestion: You know she’s gone. Noticing what the cup brings up might help us understand that lonely moment, if you want to try.

scenes.bridge: Another small trace of Ingrid brings shame about tears.
scenes.prompt: Make his reaction understandable in its context.
scenes.text: [Ashamed] I cried over her handwriting on a shopping list. How silly is that?
scenes.suggestion: That handwriting belongs to someone woven into your everyday life. Being moved by it is understandable.

scenes.bridge: Arne recalls the chair beside the table.
scenes.prompt: Ask one open question about the unclear feeling.
scenes.text: [Hesitates] There’s a feeling when I see her empty chair. I can’t quite name it.
scenes.suggestion: What do you notice as you look at that chair in your mind now?

scenes.bridge: In this moment, sadness is already apparent.
scenes.prompt: Gently explore the sadness he is noticing.
scenes.text: [Softly] There’s sadness right here when I picture the empty chair.
scenes.suggestion: Could we stay a moment with that sadness and see what you notice?

scenes.bridge: The conversation turns to sharing a day with Ingrid.
scenes.prompt: Offer a tentative guess about what the loneliness holds.
scenes.text: [Pauses] I had a story for her after the walk. It stayed in my head all evening.
scenes.suggestion: Could part of the loneliness be having nobody to share those small stories with?

scenes.bridge: He describes the ordinary things he would tell her at a distance.
scenes.prompt: Offer one close image and check whether it fits.
scenes.text: [Matter-of-fact] I have small things to tell her. Weather. Knut’s joke.
scenes.suggestion: Those little pieces of your day still turn toward her. Does that sound right?

scenes.bridge: A tender morning detail shifts toward a practical task.
scenes.prompt: Check the shift; invite a return without insisting.
scenes.text: [Soft, then brisk] I miss her at breakfast. Anyway, the kettle needs descaling.
scenes.suggestion: The kettle may need attention too. Would you like a moment with missing her before we move on?

scenes.bridge: A later moment is tearful, with Arne still present.
scenes.prompt: Follow his request for quiet company.
scenes.text: [Crying, steady breath] I miss her so much just now. Can we be quiet?
scenes.suggestion: Yes. We can be quiet together. You don’t have to find words.

scenes.bridge: Another moment brings the exhaustion of caregiving into view.
scenes.prompt: Reflect the relief and guilt without deciding what they prove.
scenes.text: [Hesitant] I felt relieved not to listen for her at night anymore. Then I felt guilty.
scenes.suggestion: The constant listening could stop, and guilt arrived alongside that relief.

scenes.bridge: Arne notices words that let love and tiredness coexist.
scenes.prompt: Help him name what he wants to keep.
scenes.text: [Softly] I can say I was tired without taking the love away.
scenes.suggestion: How would you say that in your own words, so both the love and the tiredness have a place?

scenes.bridge: The imagined session is nearly over.
scenes.prompt: Make room for tiredness and a manageable ending.
scenes.text: [Reflective] I’m glad we talked. I’m also worn out.
scenes.suggestion: Both matter as we finish. What would help with leaving today, when you’re this tired?
